rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance – criminal history ban in tenant screening
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not ask about criminal history, run criminal background checks, advertise that people with records will be excluded, or refuse to rent, end a tenancy, or charge a higher deposit or rent because of criminal history. If a landlord takes any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history, the landlord must give written notice and a chance to respond.
rules.key_value: Criminal history inquiries and use prohibited in rental housing
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing providers in Berkeley, as to current and prospective tenants, including advertising, applications, tenant selection, adding family members, deposits and rent amounts.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit as primary residence; units under a rental agreement letting owners move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation; civil damages including actual damages or three times one month's rent; punitive damages; attorneys' fees and costs; injunctive relief.

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied property of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit as primary residence
Limited exemptions for public housing / Section 8 properties
Units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back into their home per BMC 13.76.130 A.9
Existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates

notes: The document lists one rule in scope: Berkeley's Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (BMC 13.106). Effective date is left blank on purpose. The page only says City Council passed the ordinance on April 14, 2020; it does not give the date it took effect. Status is in_force because the ordinance was passed in 2020 and is still being administered as of the retrieval date. The written-notice requirement, the duty to post the Notice to Rental Applicants and Tenants, and the complaint process are all part of this one rule, so they are not separate records. Some exemptions are only named on the page, not explained; the page refers readers to the ordinance for the exact requirements of each exemption. The lifetime sex offender exemption is about the applicant, not the building, so it is listed in the exemptions text only and not as a separate exemption test. The page also mentions Measure BB registration and Rent Board fees in its news links, but gives no rule text for them, so nothing was extracted from those.
